In an email interview with Benzinga, Neamtz said investors should compare rising capital expenditures with growth in cloud and AI revenue. He identified demand, financing, power availability and customer commitments as factors shaping the next phase of AI infrastructure investment.

Backlogs, contracted commitments and capacity utilization could help indicate whether spending is becoming productive. Neamtz said companies with named customers, defined project timelines and stronger evidence of progress each quarter may be viewed differently.
“The bar rises with the size of the spend, so the companies with a plan for returns will be separated from those with only a budget,” he said.
According to the Wall Street veteran, investors could penalize companies if increased spending fails to produce visible progress over several quarters or leads to greater dependence on debt.

Washington Shift May Delay AI Projects

Neamtz said a shift in Washington after the midterms could slow federal permitting and alter energy policy, but state and local approvals and power availability will remain key constraints on AI infrastructure development.

He expects delays and project relocations rather than a reversal in demand. Projects tied to restricted locations, leveraged operators dependent on construction timelines and project-specific contractors face greater risks, while existing data center capacity and companies with secured power may be better positioned.
“We’d frame this by type of exposure, not by individual company,” he said.
Why AI Winners May Change in 2027
Neamtz described 2027 as a potential “shift in emphasis, not a reversal”, with investors asking which companies successfully converted infrastructure spending into earnings.

He also cited secured power, local opposition, financing costs, and contracted customers as considerations that may determine where projects are built and how quickly they generate returns. Neamtz added that short-term financing market fluctuations may affect the pace of growth and which companies benefit, but they won’t change the overall long-term trend.
“I believe patient funding and secured power may not be that exciting, but they are what advisors and investors ask about once the excitement fades.”

title: Exclusive: Investors Are Watching AI Revenue Growth Against CapEx as Companies Face Pressure to Prove Returns, Wall Street Veteran Says: ‘The Bar Rises With the Size of the Spend'
